title: Certificates of Deposit: sizing a grace-period top-up from the Shortfall below the jumbo threshold
content:
## Scope

When the owner of a Certificates of Deposit certificate in its grace period asks to add just enough money for the certificate to earn the jumbo bonus when it renews, this rule sizes the top-up.

## Rule

1. **Shortfall.** The Shortfall is the tier's jumbo threshold less the certificate's reconciled principal, rounded half up to 2 decimal places.
2. **Top-up.** When the Shortfall is below the tier's smallest grace add-on, the top-up is raised to the smallest grace add-on. Otherwise the top-up equals the Shortfall.
3. **Which principal.** Where the principal balance recorded on the certificate differs from the reconciled principal, the reconciled figure governs the Shortfall.

## Worked cases (illustrative threshold of 80000.00 and smallest grace add-on of 100.00, not tier values)

| Reconciled principal | Shortfall | Below the smallest grace add-on? | Top-up |
|---|---|---|---|
| 78500.00 | 1500.00 | No | 1500.00 |
| 79960.00 | 40.00 | Yes | 100.00, raised to the smallest grace add-on |
| 79900.00 | 100.00 | No, equal | 100.00 |
| 75000.00 | 5000.00 | No | 5000.00 |

A further illustration of point 3 (same illustrative figures): the certificate record shows 78000.00 while the ledger reconciles to 78500.00. The Shortfall is taken from 78500.00, giving a top-up of 1500.00; reading the recorded 78000.00 instead would give 2000.00, which the rule does not use.

## Input, judgement, output

Reconciled principal and jumbo threshold → Shortfall, rounded half up to the cent → compared with the smallest grace add-on → top-up.

## Points of judgement

**The certificate needs only 40.00 more to reach the threshold. Is 40.00 the top-up?**
No, in the illustrative case above: 40.00 is below the smallest grace add-on, so the top-up is raised to that smallest amount.

**Is the top-up ever less than the Shortfall?**
No. It equals the Shortfall, or is raised to the smallest grace add-on when the Shortfall is below it.
